name: Zvook acoustic station (Ukraine)
description: Half-metre acoustic mirror over one microphone with edge ML. Tower-mounted at 10-12 m, about 200 deg coverage, 5 km on Shahed-type OWA and 7 km on cruise missiles. Passive: it cannot be jammed or homed on.

detectRangeM.condition: up to 5000 m on a drone; 7000 m on a cruise missile
detectRangeM.source: Militarnyi, NATO Shows Interest in Ukrainian Acoustic Detection Networks for Air Defense, citing The Times

classifyRangeM.condition: classification range — No separate classification range is published. Zvook runs a multiclass model that recognises Shaheds, cruise missiles, turboprop and propeller aircraft, jet engines and helicopters; the detection event IS the class decision, so classification is modeled as available wherever detection is.
classifyRangeM.source: Ukraine develops acoustic system for determining azimuth of air targets / Militarnyi

sectorDeg.source: Militarnyi, NATO Shows Interest in Ukrainian Acoustic Detection Networks for Air Defense

rangeAccuracyM.note: A single acoustic node measures bearing at best, not range; not established by the public record.

azimuthAccuracyDeg.note: Planning factor: a single microphone behind a half-metre mirror is a bearing-class station whose beam is tens of degrees wide; 15° is recorded, coarser than the 128-microphone Discovair G2 (<10°), the only sourced acoustic figure. No Zvook bearing accuracy is published.

elevationAccuracyDeg.note: No elevation measurement is published for this acoustic node; not established by the public record.

noiseFloorDb.note: Planning factor: the detection threshold implied by this record's own refAcousticDb (100 dB at 1 m, Shahed-class) and detectRangeM (5000 m) under spherical spreading, 100 - 20 log10(5000) = 26 dB re 20 µPa, so the reported 5 km is reproduced. The half-metre acoustic mirror concentrates sound on the single microphone (Militarnyi), which with narrowband tonal processing explains a threshold below broadband ambient. No ambient condition is published for the 5 km figure.
